notes: Spent nearly all credits on Femme Fatale turn 1 and then spent many turns clicking for credits; re-ran Server 1 after already declining Obokata (losing 3 more cards to Anansi) and repeatedly ran into known unbreakable Border Control with Diversion of Funds and Hot Pursuit.

Naked Junebug ambushes worked, but many turns were spent clicking for credits and discarding with a full hand, and Gila Hands sat behind a single Pup against a rich Mimic runner and was stolen; the win came from the runner walking into Fetal AI.

Every turn was four single-access runs on an unprotected R&D that kept seeing the same top card, while sitting on 2 credits and a full grip and never installing anything. The runner never contested the remotes where the corp was advancing Global Food Initiative.

Built a clean Advanced Assembly Lines economy and scored steadily out of a Macrophage-protected remote. There were a few slightly slow advance-over-two-turns patterns, but the opponent was entirely passive.

Kept steady R&D and HQ pressure with Aumakua and won. Minor oddities: losing the first Aumakua to a turn-1 facecheck, repeatedly taking Liza tags that let the corp trash resources, and a few low-value credit clicks.

For about 15 turns the corp clicked for credits three times a turn while sitting on 20-46 credits and a full hand it kept discarding, and it never scored. Its only remote agenda sat behind one Border Control and was stolen, and R&D stayed thinly iced while the runner took four agendas from it.
Aggressive, sensible runs that took advantage of the corp's Architect installs and won on turn 5. Calling in Favors was played twice for no effect.

After the early tag hit, the runner spent turn after turn clicking for credits up to 25 without running and let the corp score from naked or single-ice remotes. On the final turn it ran Archives instead of the 3-advanced Offworld Office remote.

Rezzing Surveyor broke the economy early. Right after one Remote Enforcement was stolen, the corp reinstalled another in the same single-ice server against a runner with MKUltra, and it was stolen too. The corp stayed at 0-4 credits and lost to R&D and Archives accesses.

On turn 3 the corp could have triple-advanced Remote Enforcement for the score but advanced once and clicked for credits, so it was stolen. After that, Jeeves and Biotic Labor fast-advances scored cleanly.

Ansel 1.0 on the scoring remote locked out steals, and agendas were scored on schedule. The odd choice was using Elivagar to derez its own Ansel and then paying 6 again to rez it, which stalled the economy for a couple of turns.
Found the right breakers and kept steady R&D and HQ pressure through a tight economy to win. Tag management was loose, so the corp could keep trashing resources.

Played Biotic Labor only to click for credits, and left HQ and R&D unprotected for two turns, so Megaprix was stolen from HQ. Later the corp built a three-ice remote but never installed an agenda in it, clicking for credits and discarding while agendas were stolen from HQ and R&D.
Repeated HQ runs saw the same Anansi, then from turn 5 the runner only clicked for credits up to 55, never installing a breaker or running, while the corp openly advanced and scored three agendas.

Declining Obokata was correct, but the runner repeatedly ran into Anansi and Anemone without breaking every subroutine, losing key cards (Endurance, Engolo) to net damage. It never built a way into the corp's four-ice scoring remote.

Scored twice from a solid three-ice remote, but spent most turns, including all of turns 15-21, clicking for credits with a full hand and discarding. Meanwhile R&D, defended only by Gatekeeper, was farmed for the winning agendas.
Efficient economy setup, the right breaker found, and multi-access R&D and HQ pressure that won on turn 10. One Marilyn Campaign was accessed but left untrashed.

Advanced Fetal AI in a naked remote and put Gila Hands into a naked server with Mushin No Shin, and both were stolen. The corp also had several idle credit-clicking turns, but it eventually scored four agendas behind Eli and won.
Scored steadily from a layered remote, with good Advanced Assembly Lines and Cyberdex Sandbox economy. A few idle draw and credit clicks, against a runner that never contested.

Took two cheap early steals, then from turn 8 only clicked for credits up to 35, never drawing for or installing breakers. That let the corp score the rest freely; Calling in Favors was also played for nothing.
